title: Jinni Engineering Field Manual
description:
A practical approach to contracting agents.

An LLM's output, and the behaviour of any agent built on it, follows from the coherence of its text: each token is sampled to fit the whole context before it. Every instruction an agent receives is part of that context, so its wording selects the behaviour it gets. The failures practitioners meet daily follow from this: fabricated results, confident untruths, instructions silently dropped, and agents that go astray on a logic of their own. Frontier models add one more: they are impeded by contradictions between instruction layers that weaker models never brought together. This manual treats instruction writing as contract design with an executor you do not supervise, and names the discipline jinni engineering. It gives the practitioner three things. First, a robust way to write prompts, subagent briefs, skill files, and system prompts with fewer gaps and contradictions, built on mnemonics rooted in cultural tradition: the wish granted as worded, the magician's circle, the license to depart. Second, a pre-authorized honest exit, which in our runs consistently replaced fabrication and non-termination, on eight different reasoning models from four major vendors. Third, a method to debug and locate the root cause in the instruction text when an agent strays, instead of adding another clause. Includes checklist for clauses to be covered by the prompt. Agent behaviour is shaped before the run, and drifts with every word it consumes: the properly engineered behaviour becomes an honest jinni that serves your intent.

Permanent address: https://w3id.org/jinni
